solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Local addresses encrypted in old document

indicators.note: something encrypted has its letters scrambled into code, so these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Neighbourhood addresses have been coded and concealed inside an ancient manuscript.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encrypted' tells you to rearrange the fourteen letters of LOCAL ADDRESSES.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous ancient Jewish manuscripts found in caves at Qumran are a prime example of an old document.

clue.text: Fateful day for Brussels bureaucrats? They're monsters!

parts.note: EU men: officials of the European Union, based in Brussels
the Ides of March was the fateful day of Caesar's murder

explanation.surface: A grim day for EU officials, who are themselves cast as monsters.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth these are the Furies, avenging female spirits, so monstrous beings.

clue.text: Princess departs from South African capital

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the south means reading upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: a rani is an Indian princess or queen
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A princess leaves the capital city of South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South African capital' looks like Pretoria; in fact 'from South' says to read RANI + D upwards, and 'African capital' means money.
explanation.definitionFit: The dinar is the currency of Algeria, Libya and Tunisia, so it is African money or capital.

clue.text: Yankee eaten by horrible sea snake — that is very simple

indicators.note: eaten by means the letter goes inside the other pieces
horrible suggests the word sea is mangled into a new order

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American is devoured by a ghastly sea serpent, which is all too easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrible' makes EAS and 'eaten by' tucks the Yankee into the sea serpent; the dash then leads to the definition, so 'that is' is wordplay, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy as pie is an idiom for something extremely simple to do.

clue.text: Slim girl say vacated large pub

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so only the outside letters of say remain

parts.note: PH, public house, is an abbreviation for pub

explanation.surface: A slender young woman leaves a big pub empty, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: A sylph is a slender, graceful girl or woman, originally an air spirit.

clue.text: Artist with fantastically true storyteller

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, denotes an artist
con is Italian and Latin for with, as in musical directions

indicators.note: fantastically suggests the letters of true are rearranged wildly

explanation.surface: A painter whose tales are wildly true makes a fine storyteller.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a person who tells anecdotes skilfully and amusingly.

clue.text: Flower for all to see in large bunch?

indicators.note: in places the film rating inside the other piece

parts.note: lots means a large number or bunch
U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all audiences

explanation.surface: A flower displayed publicly among a big bouquet.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British 'universal' film classification, fit for everyone to watch.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water lily revered in Asia, an example of a flower.

clue.text: Virtuous man on field that's foreign

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the saint above the field

parts.note: ST is short for saint, a virtuous person
a range is a field or scope

explanation.surface: A good man out on a field that seems alien.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange can mean foreign or unfamiliar, as in a strange land.

clue.text: Church area straddling border in war zone

indicators.note: straddling means sitting either side of something, so the border goes between

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: A church district on a frontier caught up in fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimean peninsula was the scene of the Crimean War and later conflict, a war zone.

clue.text: Right country for Catholic

parts.note: Oman is a country on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: Picking the right nation for a Catholic believer to live in.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman Catholic is commonly called a Roman, after the church centred on Rome.

clue.text: Lawyer indeed permitted to be with men

parts.note: so can mean indeed, as in 'it is so!'
licit means lawful or permitted
OR (other ranks) stands for ordinary soldiers, i.e. men

explanation.surface: A lawyer who is indeed allowed to spend time in the company of men.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, 'other ranks', is the military term for soldiers below officer level, a crossword staple for 'men'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a solicitor is the kind of legal professional who advises clients and prepares cases.

clue.text: Island in unimportant American state

parts.note: minor means of little importance
CA is the postal abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: An island located within some insignificant US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Minorca, or Menorca, is one of the Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean, belonging to Spain.

clue.text: Chinese gong not initially practical

parts.note: the Han are the majority ethnic group of China
a gong is slang for a medal; the DSO is the Distinguished Service Order

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word not

explanation.surface: A Chinese gong that, oddly, is impractical at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gong' is British slang for a medal or decoration, here the DSO, a military honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A hands-on approach is practical and involves direct personal involvement rather than theory.

clue.text: Writer initially unnerved in old British colony

indicators.note: in places the picked letter inside the name of the colony

parts.note: Aden, in today's Yemen, was a British colony until 1967

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word unnerved

explanation.surface: A writer who was at first rattled when posted to a former British possession.
explanation.definitionFit: W. H. Auden was an Anglo-American poet, so he is an example of a writer.

clue.text: Managed to get raise with share account

indicators.note: raise in a down clue lifts the word upwards, reversing it

parts.note: ran means managed, as in running a business
a ration is a share or allowance

explanation.surface: Someone managed to obtain a pay rise along with a stake.
explanation.definitionFit: A narration is a spoken or written account of events.

clue.text: Gentle energy put through seed line

parts.note: a pea is the seed of a pod plant

indicators.note: put through suggests threading one letter into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: a cable is a line or wire
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Some soft energy routed down a seed-sowing line, like a gardening gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone peaceable is mild and disinclined to quarrel, close in sense to gentle.

clue.text: Unmanned gun

definitions.meaning: working by itself with no human operator
a self-loading firearm that keeps firing while the trigger is held

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes self-operating machinery and is also a noun for a self-loading weapon.

clue.text: Dreadful batons aid sole punishment

indicators.note: dreadful suggests the letters are in a terrible mess, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Awful truncheons assist in punishing the feet.
explanation.definitionFit: The bastinado is a torture of beating the soles of the feet with a stick.

clue.text: Orders at intervals to take necessary back up

indicators.note: at intervals asks for every other letter of Orders, here the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: urgent means pressing or necessary

explanation.surface: Instructions given periodically to grab what's required and support it.
explanation.definitionFit: Resurgent means rising again, i.e. coming back up after a decline.

clue.text: Go hard round bends — this driver might!

definitions.text: Go hard round bends — this driver might!

indicators.note: bends hints at twisting the letters about, so the pieces are rearranged

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A reckless motorist would take the corners at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both gives the wordplay and describes the driver.
explanation.definitionFit: A road hog is an inconsiderate, aggressive driver who speeds and takes up the road.

clue.text: Devotee overthrows an emperor

indicators.note: overthrows suggests turning things upside down, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: the indefinite article an is written as A
a tsar was an emperor of Russia

explanation.surface: A zealous follower topples an emperor in a revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rastafarian follower, short form Rasta, is a devotee of Haile Selassie.

clue.text: Woman hiding information makes plan

indicators.note: hiding means the woman's name conceals the other piece within it

parts.note: Ada is a woman's name
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A woman keeps the facts secret to make her scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list of items to be dealt with, a plan of business.

clue.text: Light taking half-year to fix

indicators.note: half asks for one half of the word year, here its second two letters

parts.note: to clamp is to fix firmly in place

explanation.surface: A lamp that needs six months to repair.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc lamp produces brilliant light from an electric arc, so it is a kind of light.

clue.text: Copper to restrain attractive girl

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to tie someone is to restrain them

explanation.surface: A police officer moves to detain a pretty young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman but gives the chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutie is informal for a charming or good-looking person.

clue.text: Genuine broadcasting contract

indicators.note: broadcasting signals that the word is spoken out on air

parts.note: to pucker is to contract into wrinkles

explanation.surface: A real deal for a radio or TV station.
explanation.definitionFit: Pukka, from Hindi, is British informal for authentic or first-class.

clue.text: Feature in West shows robot

indicators.note: in places the facial feature within the actress's first name

parts.note: Mae West was the American film actress
the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A film starring Mae West showcases a robot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' looks like a direction, but it is the actress Mae West.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot is an automated device, a kind of machine.

clue.text: Daily Mail's leader to delight?

parts.note: a daily is British for a cleaning woman, also called a char

indicators.note: leader asks for the first letter of Mail's

explanation.surface: Is the Daily Mail's editorial meant to please?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily Mail' looks like the British newspaper, but a 'daily' is a cleaner who comes in each day.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone is to please or enchant them.

clue.text: Success with gate — thus getting out?

parts.note: a hit is a success
a wicket is a small gate

explanation.surface: Escaping after a triumph involving a gate.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman is out 'hit wicket' if they knock over their own stumps; a wicket is also an old word for a small gate.
explanation.definitionFit: Hit wicket is one of the ways a batsman is dismissed in cricket, an example of getting out.

clue.text: Leader to advise duke about campaign medal

indicators.note: Leader to asks for the first letter of the word advise

parts.note: a campaign can be a war

explanation.surface: A chief counsels a duke regarding a military medal.
explanation.definitionFit: A medal is a kind of award given for merit or service.

clue.text: Fresh meat abundant in peace camp

parts.note: green means fresh or new
ham is meat
common means plentiful or abundant

explanation.surface: Plenty of fresh meat available at an activists' camp.
explanation.walkthrough: Greenham Common in Berkshire, England, was the site of a women's peace camp protesting nuclear missiles in the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: The women's protest at the RAF base there became famous as a peace camp.
